issues.description: Method getTotalNumberOfStudents: The problem statement (task description and UML) requires a no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (inscribed + guest). The template has a TODO placeholder for this method (no signature present, but the task text and UML indicate a no-arg int method). The solution implementation declares public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) — i.e., it adds a boolean parameter. This parameter mismatch between the solution and the problem/template will confuse students about the required signature, cause inconsistencies in how other methods should call it (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor in the solution call this parameterized variant), and can lead to failing tests or compilation issues when graders/tests expect the no-argument method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution conform to the specification: change the solution method signature to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() (no parameters) and have it return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents. Update any internal calls in the solution (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to call the no-arg method. Alternatively, if the boolean parameter was intentional, update the problem statement, UML and template to document the new parameter and its semantics (includeGuests) so all artifacts agree.

issues.description: The exercise specification (problem statement and UML) requires a no-argument method named getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns an int. The template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) leaves a TODO for implementing getTotalNumberOfStudents (no signature provided), while the solution implementation defines a different method signature: getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). Because the solution's method is named the same but has a boolean parameter, students reading the problem will expect a no-arg method and may not find it in the provided solution/template — causing confusion about the required API and blocking them when they search for or call getTotalNumberOfStudents() without arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation with the problem/UML by adding a public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() no-argument method that returns the total number of students. If the boolean option to include/exclude guest students is desired, add an overloaded method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) in addition to the no-arg version, or update the problem statement and UML to explicitly specify the boolean parameter and its semantics.
